correctness.rationale: For each clique the exact update is obtained by separately comparing one-neighbour counts for distinguished and nondistinguished vertices, including ties and small n=3,4 boundaries. Odd cliques become consensus by time two; an even clique at half occupancy complements its nondistinguished vertices and copies the opposite bridge, and remains critical exactly while bridge bits disagree. These exhaustive cases prove the sharp 2/4/5 bounds, classify all fixed and 2-periodic states, and permit exact binomial counting of each maximal-depth stratum. The bundled independent direct-mask simulator checks all 254016 labelled configurations across 36 graphs, including all boundary parity cases, but proof is general and does not rely on computation.

value.rationale: A single bridge linking two dense communities is a canonical bottleneck graph, and the result supplies an exact infinite-family relaxation phase diagram. The sharp 2/4/5 parity transition, exact rare critical configurations, algebraic 1/(π sqrt(ab)) prevalence, and complete exceptional 2-cycle count explain a nontrivial time-lag mechanism at the interface; these facts are not generic consequences of eventual period two and are more than textbook restatements or isolated numerical tables.
